bib.title: Rethinking with Retrieval: Faithful Large Language Model Inference

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Rethinking with Retrieval: Faithful Large Language Model Inference", Hangfeng He, Hongming Zhang, Dan Roth; arXiv:2301.00303v1 preprint, 31 Dec 2022.
COVERAGE: 55,664 of 55,664 chars read (main text, references, appendix A.1-A.5, prompt tables 6 and 8). No gaps. Figure 2 is a plot, so only its axes were extracted, not its values. The note's frontmatter lists arXiv 2204.06092, 2305.14627 and others, but NOT 2301.00303, so this would be a new source for the note.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- RR (rethinking with retrieval) beats every baseline on all three reasoning tasks with no training or fine-tuning. It is a post-processing step: sample CoT paths, retrieve evidence per reasoning step, pick the prediction best supported by that evidence.
  number: StrategyQA 77.73 vs self-consistency 73.36 vs CoT 65.94; TempQuestions 39.05 vs 37.28 vs 33.14; INFOTABS 84.83 vs 84.00 vs 83.33
  setup: GPT-3 text-davinci-002, 256 max tokens; CoT/few-shot at temperature 0; self-consistency and RR sample 10 outputs at temperature 0.7 (9 for StrategyQA). Accuracy for StrategyQA and INFOTABS, exact match for temporal. StrategyQA dev set has 229 examples. Temporal eval has 169 examples. INFOTABS eval has 1,200 hypotheses.
  quote: "Rethinking with retrieval 77.73 39.05 84.83" (Table 1); "Self-consistency 73.36 37.28 84.00"; "Chain-of-thought prompting 65.94 33.14 83.33"
  where: Table 1, section 4.5
- Retrieving per decomposed reasoning step beats retrieving with the original query.
  number: commonsense 77.73 vs 73.36; the second column of Table 3 is labelled "Tabular" but the text says it is temporal, 39.05 vs 36.69. The query-based commonsense score equals the self-consistency score, which suggests no gain over no retrieval.
  setup: same as above, other parts unchanged
  quote: "Query-based 73.36 36.69 / Decomposition-based 77.73 39.05" (Table 3); "the results for these experiments are poor for both commonsense and temporal reasoning, indicating the importance of using decomposition-based retrieval"
  where: Sec 5.2, Table 3. Note the Table 3 header/text inconsistency (Tabular vs temporal).
- BM25 beat dense retrieval for the StrategyQA Wikipedia step.
  number: BM25 77.73, DPR 58.52, BM25+DPR 77.29
  setup: StrategyQA with Wikipedia, top-10 paragraphs per explanation sentence, then MPNet picks the most similar one, then an NLI model scores it
  quote: "The performance of BM25, DPR, and BM25+DPR were 77.73%, 58.52%, and 77.29%, respectively"
  where: App A.3
- With gold evidence paragraphs, RR raises both accuracy and the faithfulness of the explanation. Faithfulness is an NLI-based factual-consistency score.
  number: CoT 65.94 accuracy / 38.73 faithfulness; basic without voting 76.86 / 50.02; Variant I (fact selection) 78.60 / 54.11; Variant II (fact generation) 78.60 / 54.54. Basic with voting reaches 79.91.
  setup: StrategyQA with the provided evidence paragraphs as the knowledge, GPT-3, final step done by UnifiedQA-v2. Faithfulness uses the NLI model of Nie et al. 2020 in place of T5-11B.
  quote: "CoT prompting 65.94 38.73 / Basic (w/o voting) 76.86 50.02 / Variant I 78.60 54.11 / Variant II 78.60 54.54" (Table 5); "The incorporation of a voting mechanism leads to an increased prediction accuracy of 79.91% for the basic approach."
  where: Sec 5.3, Table 5
- Answer accuracy depends heavily on the quality of the supporting facts handed to the final answerer.
  number: GPT-3 CoT scores 65.94 with empty facts, 76.42 with generated facts, 91.70 with gold facts. UnifiedQA scores 58.95 / 78.60 / 90.83. GPT-3 zero-shot scores 58.08 / 69.87 / 81.66.
  setup: StrategyQA. In the empty-facts condition the answerer gets no facts. The gold and generated facts come from the StrategyQA annotations and from Variant II.
  quote: "UnifiedQA performs better at inference with generated facts, while GPT-3 with CoT prompting performs better with empty or gold facts. This suggests that UnifiedQA is more robust to noisy inputs compared to GPT-3."
  where: App A.5, Table 7; Sec 5.3
- Model failures come in two kinds: wrong supporting facts, and wrong inference from correct facts. Both occur even when the model picks the right angle on the question.
  number: none
  setup: qualitative examples from GPT-3 CoT on StrategyQA (Lil Jon / "Get Low" instead of "Yeah"; Mount Fuji 3,776 m vs Sea of Japan "about 3,741 meters deep" when the true max depth is 3,742 m and the model concludes "would not stick out")
  quote: "GPT-3 may occasionally produce incorrect supporting facts for its explanations or make incorrect inferences for its predictions, despite generally being able to identify suitable perspectives."
  where: Sec 5.1, Table 2
- For tabular reasoning, the table itself (background knowledge) carries nearly all of the gain. WordNet/ConceptNet add little.
  number: external only 79.92, background only 84.75, both 84.83
  setup: INFOTABS, GPT-3
  quote: "External 79.92 / Background 84.75 / Background + External 84.83" (Table 4)
  where: Sec 5.2, Table 4
- The gain also shows in smaller models. Variant II beats CoT on both accuracy and faithfulness across OPT 1.3B to 30B plus GPT-3 175B. The exact values are in Figure 2 and were not extracted.
  number: none (plot only)
  setup: OPT 1.3B/2.7B/6.7B/13B/30B and GPT-3 175B, same setup as sec 5.3
  quote: "our proposed method (Variant II) consistently outperforms CoT prompting in terms of both prediction accuracy and the faithfulness of explanations, even when using smaller LMs."
  where: Sec 5.4, Fig 2
- Faithfulness score (the mechanism). Each path is scored f_KB per explanation sentence from MPNet similarity M, NLI entailment E and contradiction C. The prediction is chosen by summing the scores over the paths that agree on it (Eq. 1).
  number: thresholds Tm=0.5, Te=0.6, Tc=0.99
  setup: three f_KB variants. Function (1) is used for commonsense and tabular, (2) for temporal because the contradiction scores are unreliable on templated sentences, and (3) with gold evidence.
  quote: "fKB(R) = ∑s∈S[M (s)×(M (s) >= Tm) + E(s)× (M (s) < T m)− C(s)]"
  where: App A.2; Eq. 1 in Sec 3

LIMITS
- GPT-3 text-davinci-002 only (OPT only in the scaling plot). Only three reasoning tasks, with small eval sets (169 temporal examples, 229 StrategyQA). No variance, seeds or significance tests were seen. Gains over self-consistency are small on temporal (+1.77) and tabular (+0.83).
- The method is post-hoc. It needs N sampled paths (10, or 9 for StrategyQA) plus a retriever, MPNet and NLI calls per reasoning sentence, so it costs more. The paper reports no cost or latency numbers.
- The knowledge bases are matched to the task: Wikipedia for commonsense, Wikidata for temporal, tables plus WordNet/ConceptNet for tabular. This is not open-domain RAG in the modern prompt-stuffing sense. The authors concede the work is in its early stages and say only that they plan to explore variations.
- The faithfulness metric is an NLI proxy, not human judgment. The Variant I/II experiments use gold evidence paragraphs. The temporal task needs a different f_KB because the NLI contradiction scores were unreliable.
- Dated: the models are 2022-era (GPT-3 davinci-002, OPT). Argmax over agreeing paths ignores the tokens-versus-attention concerns that later work raises. The paper makes no claim about context length, though it says RR is "not limited by the input length of LLMs".

BUILDS ON: Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022); self-consistency (Wang et al., 2022); kNN-LM (Khandelwal et al., 2020, named as the closest related work); Nye et al. (2021) neuro-symbolic consistency; retrieval-augmented LMs (Lewis et al., 2020; Guu et al., 2020; Borgeaud et al., 2021); BM25 via Pyserini (Lin et al., 2021; Karpukhin et al., 2020); MPNet (Song et al., 2020); the adversarial NLI model (Nie et al., 2020); UnifiedQA-v2 (Khashabi et al., 2022); the TRUE factual-consistency metric (Honovich et al., 2022); StrategyQA (Geva et al., 2021).

CODE: none in the paper (repo at github.com/HornHehhf/RR). Eq. 1: P̂ = argmax over Pi of sum_i 1(Pi = P) * f_KB(Ri). Appendix A.2 has the f_KB formulas, quoted above.

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.1-2), pipeline (a) standard prompt, (b) CoT, (c) RR retrieves per reasoning step. Fig 2 (p.6), accuracy and faithfulness against model size, 1.3B to 175B, CoT versus RR Variant II. Fig 2 values are not in the text. I did not run the caption script, as the captions were already in the extraction.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Ligature and spacing glitches in the extraction. Table 3's column header says "Tabular" while the prose says temporal. Fig 2 numeric values are not recoverable from the text. The target note 06 (read only to line 60) does not currently list arXiv 2301.00303, and the "Why RAG works" section is about attention, so the fit is loose. The closest fit is a faithfulness or grounding section. Cite as sharpens or new, the caller decides.
